Maxima-lsp

Posted on July 28, 2026
Tags: maxima

The language server protocol the standard way to get deterministic help with code. I use neovim to interact with R languageserver, clangd (c or c++), basedpyright (python), rust-analyzer or haskell-language-server. In any of those languages I use the same keybindings to get information or modify code

  1. looking up documentation (hover)
  2. renaming an identifier
  3. jump-to-definition
  4. jump-to-use
  5. factor out sub-expression (common subexpression elimination – CSE)
  6. inline (unCSE)
  7. inlay inferred types
  8. type, syntax errors

maxima didn’t have a LSP. There are generic language servers that can usually get 2,3,4,8 right. None of the LSPs do 5&6 well. LSP is difficult to learn because there can be too many layers written by different people that work together on a single task. For example neovim used to use coc.nvim used language server protocol to request haskell language server to ask retrie to make changes. When it doesn’t work correctly, where is the mistake? Which layer should I ask for a trace of what happened? Who has to change to fix the bug? Thankfully there’s common understanding of what the system is supposed to do.

I’ll describe the process of putting maxima-lsp together. At first I tried the lsp package, because this is used by haskell-language-server and futhark. But I stopped at this point. I was surprised that the lsp package will not generate the initialize response which tells the editor (neovim) what it is allowed to send. The LSP.Handlers looks similar to the haskell servant library can generate a description of the API from the code that usually responds to that API. At least in principle the type checker could confirm that the client handles all responses it requests. The final version of the initialize response is here for comparison. Starting at the main in each version, look how many steps reach the actual renaming logic:

With lsp library, main runs a LSP.ServerDefinition which configures their main loop with 8 different values/callbacks. The staticHandlers includes the handleRename2 function that uses lens-regex-pcre to apply the renaming, and then callback’s callback needs to see the results packaged up into a Either (LSP.TResponseError LSP.Method_TextDocumentRename) (LSP.WorkspaceEdit LSP.|? LSP.Null).

In the current version, main sets up the server state and then has a loop to read requests and write the responses. rename pattern matches on the json Value described by textDocument/rename. Following that documentation has similar indirection to lsp, except lsp adds an extra newtype around row/column/uri values. Another difference is that interface RenameParams extends TextDocumentPositionParams, WorkDoneProgressParams { are missing from the latest code. In the first version haskell imagine support for wildcards for constructor names, By this I mean having _ stand in for the constructor(s) with the right number of fields. For example the language might let you make progress without naming Just:

data Maybe a = Nothing | Just a
maybe :: b -> (a -> b) -> Maybe a -> b
maybe _ ab (_ a) = ab a
maybe b _   _    = b

. I only need to know the field names and use the values bound to the field names at types that can be parsed from the json matched using Pun.json.
